To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The incorporation of 32P into cytoplasmic phosphoproteins is increased after exposure of mice or rats to 600 or 2500 R, total body x-irradiation, respectively.
the relative turnover of nucleic acid phosphorus in the liver was altered after total body X- irradiation.
the incorporation of radioactive phosphorus into DNA and nuclear RNA of rat and mouse liver was depressed after exposure to total body X- irradiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of total-body X-irradiaton upon the relative turnover of nucleic acid phosphorus.
the effect of total-body X-irradiations upon the relative turnover of nucleic acid phosphorus.
the effect of total body X- irradiation on the incorporation of P ^{32} into nucleic acid phosphorus in the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
total-body X-irradiated animals have an increased cPNA turnover and a decreased DNA turnover.
the relative turnover of nucleic acid phosphorus is altered by X-irradiaton, and the effect on DNA is opposite to the effect on cPNA.
total body irradiation of the rat and mouse causes an increase in the rate of turnover of cytoplasmic phospholipids and phosphoproteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in all instances of increased cPNA synthesis the increase was due to a relative increase of cPNA synthesis, since the total amount of cPNA per liver did not increase.
the increased cPNA synthesis may be a result of the increased synthesis of protein in the liver.
in the rat the increase in cPNAsynthesis is a compensating mechanism for the decrease in DNA synthesis, and that in the mouse the decrease in cPNAsyn-thesis is not a compensating mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
total body x-irradiation causes a relative increase in the turnover of cytoplasmic nucleic acid phosphorus.
the effects of radiation on the synthesis of nucleic acids are complex and cannot be understood in terms of simple models.
total-body X-irradiated rats have increased cPNA specific activities.
